statements.text: Combined with causal closure, the knowledge argument supports epiphenomenalism about qualia: the phenomenal information Mary acquires concerns properties that are not physical, and those properties have no effects in the physical world. Jackson was for a time one of the few philosophers who embraced this view.

sources.quote: When combined with the traditional arguments (Pro) given above, it becomes a potent source of support for epiphenomenalism.

sources.locator: section 5, 'The Dualist View About the Knowledge Argument'
sources.quote: Until some time ago Jackson was one of the very few philosophers who embraced epiphenomenalism.
